subject.title: [security] WebVNC handoff persists share credentials as plaintext Durable Object records

question: Which secret boundary should WebVNC credential handoff storage use so Durable Object storage readers cannot recover active VNC credentials without the handoff ticket?
rationale: The source-confirmed issue is security-sensitive, and choosing ticket-bound sealing versus a deployment or broker secret changes Crabbox's supported threat model and operational behavior.

options.title: Ticket-bound sealing
options.body: Make the random handoff ticket necessary to decrypt the stored credential payload while preserving one-time consume and TTL semantics.

options.title: Deployment-secret sealing
options.body: Encrypt the handoff payload with a coordinator secret outside Durable Object storage, accepting that broker runtime secret access remains sufficient to decrypt.

options.title: Document TTL-only storage
options.body: Treat plaintext five-minute storage as accepted hardening debt and document that storage readers are inside the broker trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Ticket-bound sealing
recommendation.body: Make the random handoff ticket necessary to decrypt the stored credential payload while preserving one-time consume and TTL semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The current handoff implementation and recent WebVNC hardening history both trace to this owner candidate.
